record.content_text:
The diagram shows that the transversal $GH$ intersects the parallel lines $CD$ and $EF$.

The intersecting lines create angles. Some of these angles are labelled.

Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-0_046.png

If the two lines are parallel, the four angles around the first intersection are the same as the four angles around the second intersection. We can use this to determine the unknown angles.

- $\hat{x}$ is in the same position as the angle of $65^{\circ}$, so $x = 65^{\circ}$.
- $\hat {x}$ and $\hat{y}$ are angles on a straight line, so $\hat{y} = 115^{\circ}$.
- $\hat {x}$ and $\hat{z}$ are vertically opposite angles, so $\hat{z} = 65^{\circ}$.

We can fill in the sizes of all the angles on the diagram.

Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-1_025.png

We give special names to the angles formed by two parallel lines and a transversal. There are three types of angles that you should learn to recognise:

**Corresponding angles**: Corresponding angles are in matching positions on the parallel lines. They are on the same side of the parallel lines, and on the same side of the transversal.

If we colour the lines that make corresponding angles, we will see an "F" shape. This helps us to identify corresponding angles.

Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-028.png

Corresponding angles are equal, but only if the lines cut by the transversal are parallel.

**Co-interior angles**: Co-interior angles are both inside the parallel lines, and on the same side of the transversal.

If we colour the lines that make co-interior angles, we will see a "U" shape. This helps us identify co-interior angles.

Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-029.png

Co-interior angles add up to $180^{\circ}$, but only if the lines cut by the transversal are parallel.

**Alternate angles**: Alternate angles are both inside the parallel lines, but on different sides of the transversal.

If we colour the lines that make alternate angles, we will see an "N" shape. This helps us identify alternate angles.

Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-030.png

Alternate angles are equal, but only if the lines cut by the transversal are parallel.

To help you remember these angles, think of **Maths is FUN!**

If two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, then:

- **F**: corresponding angles are equal
- **U**: co-interior angles are supplementary
- **N**: alternate angles are equal

record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 15.4: Identify angles at intersecting lines

The diagram shows line $IJ$ intersecting line $EF$. The intersecting lines create four different angles. These angles are labelled $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\delta$, and $x$.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-0_043.png]

1. Which angle or angles are supplementary to $\hat{x}$?
record.answer_text:
Supplementary angles form a straight line.

$\hat{\beta}$ and $\hat{x}$ are supplementary.

$\hat{\delta}$ and $\hat{x}$ are supplementary.

record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 15.4: Identify angles at intersecting lines

The diagram shows line $IJ$ intersecting line $EF$. The intersecting lines create four different angles. These angles are labelled $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\delta$, and $x$.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-0_043.png]

4. Say whether the following statement is true or false:

$$
\hat{x} = \hat{\alpha}
$$
record.answer_text:
$\hat{x}$ and $\hat {\alpha}$ are vertically opposite angles and vertically opposite angles are equal.

The statement is true.

closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.rationale: The textbook explicitly teaches co-interior angles alongside corresponding and alternate angles, and includes an exercise item for recognising them. The canonical curriculum list names alternate and corresponding angles but omits co-interior angles.
